Eleven read routes, each as a person and as an agent: GET /api/v1/issues/{key}, /issues/{key}/artifacts, /issues/{key}/asks?state=all, /issues/{key}/events, /issues/{key}/summary, /issues/{key}/references, /artifacts/{id} and /issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug} (finding 1's own routes, added this round), /artifacts/{id}/asks, /artifacts/{id}/references, /projects/{key}/artifacts and /inbox. Three binaries read the one database, each restored from a kept seed template so the rows are identical: main 5dc21cb9 (the fork point), cd2e246d (the head the review was written at) and 5530be49.
proof.command: python3 seed.py keys.json, then for each side ./restore.sh bin/dispatch-<side> && python3 dump2.py keys.json r4b-<side>, then diff the manifests. The seed is 228 issues written through the HTTP API alone, this round carrying approvals in every state the lookup answers: 40 documents with an open approval request, 20 approved, and 11 of the awaiting ones given a later version on top so their approval reads stale. Scripts under the pod's $TMPDIR/t512; the procedure is in its ROUND4.md.

All three manifests are the same file: sha256 ef7f535f2fb981bcca6c26274ef7d3ea6e114522f64b1c50ba3d600ca61dc3e1 at main 5dc21cb9, at cd2e246d and at 5530be49. proof.negativeControl: Two mutants of this head, each built and run through the same comparison. (1) queueApprovals with the open-approval-request statement not queued: 320 of 8,086 answers differ. proof.observed: The probe's lines are identical at cd2e246d and at 5530be49: sequential open=201 state=awaiting version=1 waiting_on=human and the second request 409 on all four; concurrent on twelve documents 201 x8 and 409 x4 (the four that already had a request from the sequential wave); sixteen at once on one document 409 x16; the contended document reads back state=awaiting waiting_on=human; the shared pool holds 0 connections with 437 returned; and all twelve documents read back awaiting. No wave came near its 90 s bound. The implementer's committed test passes under -race. The 409s are the route's own behaviour at an unchanged version, not a defect, and they are the same on both sides.
